headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0218 — This PDF is too big for SMTO to work with

html:
SMTO-EXE-0218 — This PDF is too big for SMTO to work with

GUID: 02da8763-d861-5a8c-a1aa-e7fa6733fa19
Slug: pdf-too-large
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: pdf

What happened

  • The PDF is larger than SMTO can handle in one request, has more than 2,000 pages, or has no pages at all. SMTO stopped without making a new file, and your original is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the file's size and page count. Each PDF must be under 64 MB and 2,000 pages, and all files in one request together under 128 MB. These are SMTO's fixed limits for one PDF request, so a file over them will always stop here.
  2. If the file is over the limit, split it into smaller PDFs with another PDF app, then ask SMTO to work on one part at a time. SMTO can't open a file that is over the limit, so it has to be made smaller before SMTO can use it.
  3. If you're combining PDFs or adding pages, do it in smaller batches, for example two files at a time, so the result stays under 2,000 pages. The new PDF must also fit the limits, not only the files you start with.
  4. If the PDF shows no pages when you open it, get a fresh copy from wherever it came from, then try again. A PDF with zero pages needs a working copy; making it smaller won't help.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the request and shows the new PDF or the information you asked for.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's size and page count, to the person who manages SMTO. These limits can't be raised in settings, so don't keep resending the same large file.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway PDF worker rejected the request because an input or output PDF exceeded the size limits (64 MiB per file, 128 MiB in total) or the document had zero pages or more than 2,000 pages.

What this means

  • Input or generated PDF bytes exceeded per-file/aggregate bounds, a transformation would exceed page capacity, or a parsed document contained zero or more than 2,000 pages. PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.

Why this can happen

  • Input or generated PDF bytes exceeded per-file/aggregate bounds, a transformation would exceed page capacity, or a parsed document contained zero or more than 2,000 pages.

How to diagnose it

  • Check 64 MiB per file, 128 MiB aggregate and a valid one-to-2,000-page document, including proposed merged output.

How to fix it

  • Compare the inputs and planned outputs with MAX_FILE (64 MiB per file), MAX_OUTPUT (128 MiB total for inputs and for outputs) and MAX_PAGES (2,000) in src/gateway_core/pdf/contract.py; merge and insert_pages also fail when the combined page count exceeds 2,000. These limits are fixed, so split the work into smaller requests or replace a zero-page document with a valid PDF.
  • Use supported bounded PDFs and outputs; a zero-page input needs a valid document rather than further size reduction.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a smaller PDF or fewer output pages. Each file is limited to 64 MiB, aggregate bytes to 128 MiB, and documents to 2,000 pages.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended complete bounded input/output meets valid size and page-count requirements.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • PDF parsing and OCR remain local bounded operations on the selected Gateway. Outputs are separate create-only files/artifacts; diagnostic rendering adds no reads, credential recovery, model calls or automatic retries.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
